video_title: Evan Turner Critiques His Former Team's Cost-Cutting Moves | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dunden is applying a Carolina Hurricanes-style playbook to the Portland Trail Blazers
quotes.excerpt: he is now doing in Portland. He got to Carolina and he shook up the front office.
quotes.quote: I think he is running the Carolina Hurricanes playbook down to the last detail. Everything that he did in Carolina when he took over, he is now doing in Portland. He got to Carolina and he shook up the front office. The head coach was gone within a matter of months, the general manager was gone. Efficiency is the term for some of the cost-cutting, but he gutted some of the personnel in that office. He also had a similar battle with the city of Raleigh over some of the money for the stadium that he is having right now with the city of Portland. But he has taken the Carolina Hurricanes playbook and he has dropped it into Portland and on the Trail Blazers.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Small-market NBA teams must prioritize investing in front-office brain power
quotes.excerpt: one of the things that makes teams successful, small-market especially teams successful, is the investment they make
quotes.quote: Does the model that was successful in hockey work in basketball? Because even if you pour money into the team and are willing to go into the tax aprons, one of the things that makes teams successful, small-market especially teams successful, is the investment they make in brain power. The money they spend on front-office work, on scouting, all the things that make some of these small-market teams great. Oklahoma City is great because of Sam Presti at the top, but they also have a deep staff of basketball operations, a detailed scouting department. They invest a lot of money in personnel.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' investment in Sean Elliott and other staff paid off
quotes.excerpt: they paid a lot of money to get him out of Dallas. And he turned out to
quotes.quote: Look at San Antonio. Sean Elliott last year with the Spurs, how valuable was he? They paid a lot of money to get him out of Dallas. And he turned out to be a difference maker on the bench for Mitch Johnson. Just ask Mitch Johnson, ask Victor Wembanyama, ask Stephon Castle, ask Dylan Harper. These guys benefited greatly from the Spurs going out and investing in one of the best basketball minds in the assistant ranks at that time.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dunden's overconfidence in his hockey-based model for the Trail Blazers
quotes.excerpt: you think Dunden is kind of overconfident because he is like, hey, if I am willing to
quotes.quote: You think Dunden is kind of overconfident because he is like, hey, if I am willing to go into that first or second apron, what are we talking about? Is there a way scale in the sense, especially when you look at Portland. You are not getting a free agent in Portland unless you are throwing them an arm and a leg to go with it. So when it comes down and Dunden is like, hey, if I take all this money in this run in and I am spending it on the product, and no matter what, whether we sit here or not, and I am telling you I got Phil Jackson and we got the best practice facility, nobody is coming to Portland for that regardless.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dunden's questions about why Christian Wood is out of the NBA
quotes.excerpt: he was asking some personnel about why Christian Wood was no longer in the NBA
quotes.quote: Somebody told me recently that he was asking some personnel about why Christian Wood was no longer in the NBA. Because I think he looks at the numbers that Christian Wood has put up and sees like a guy that could potentially, in Dallas he was like nearly a double-double guy, and he will give you numbers. But the reality is, as you and I both know, Christian Wood is just proven to be not a winning player.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Building a successful NBA team is harder than ever before
quotes.excerpt: building an NBA team, successful one, has never been harder. It's never been harder because even if
quotes.quote: Building an NBA team, successful one, has never been harder. It's never been harder because even if you find the magical elixir, within a year or two you have to break it up because these guys get too expensive. Look at what Boston has done, look at what Oklahoma City is now doing. Eventually San Antonio is going to get there. Everybody has to shake up their roster because of these second aprons. You have to have a full and robust staff in your front office.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Connor's deep knowledge of basketball and the limitations of analytics
quotes.excerpt: Dan knows 10-year-olds. Like when you see Christian Wood to show up and like why don't analytics
quotes.quote: Shout out to my man Dan Connor in Portland. I hope he is still there. People that just know basketball. When you show up, Dan knows 10-year-olds. Like when you see Christian Wood to show up and like why don't analytics work with him? It's little things that we always argue. Like analytics is cute, but it doesn't break down who the person is. Christian Wood, shout out to Christian, was amazing analytically. And you have to show up and be like, hey, historically he's never been able to be depended on. You want to know why here?
